item.title: EMMM Day
item.description:
Monday, 12 October 2026

Kangaroo Point Bridge will be lit Red to support EMMM Day

EMMM Day raises awareness of the harm experienced by children and young people when safe and meaningful family relationships are damaged, restricted, or severed through coercive post-separation family dynamics.
The day supports public education about psychological and relational pressures that can affect children, including repeated negative messaging, distorted information, fear-based claims, loyalty demands, and emotional expectations that interfere with a child's identity, attachment, development, and family connections.
It recognises the impact on children, displaced parents, grandparents, siblings, and extended family members, including ambiguous loss and disenfranchised grief, while making clear that genuine safety concerns, family violence, abuse, and neglect must be carefully assessed and never minimised. Its purpose is to promote early recognition, child protection, critical thinking, and safe, healthy family relationships wherever appropriate.

This Light Up is organised by: Eeny Meeny Miney Mo Foundation Ltd

item.title: Helena's House
item.description:
Tuesday, 13 October 2026

Kangaroo Point Bridge will be lit Teal and Gold to support Helena's House

Helena McIlwain passed away on the 13th of October 2019 from a pulmonary embolism. Helena worked in disabilities while studying biomedical science at QUT. Her dream was to be in the medical world so she could help and support people with a disability. A house will be named in her honour. Helena's House, which is now being built through hard work and fundraising. A unique space where our young people will practice independent living skills and develop the emotional resilience needed to gradually transition from the family home to a life of their choice, with people they know. Helena’s House will support our children’s essential next step on their path to a more independent life – one that is safe, secure and guaranteed.

This Light Up is organised by: Bestlife

item.title: National Carer's Week
item.description:
Wednesday, 14 October 2026

Kangaroo Point Bridge will be lit Blue to celebrate National Carer's Week

National Carers Week is a time to recognise, celebrate and raise awareness of the more than 3 million Australians who provide unpaid care to a family member or friend. The 2026 theme, “Care for a carer: Making carers visible,” shines a light on the invaluable contribution of unpaid carers and encourages all Australians to recognise, celebrate and care for the carers in their families, workplaces and communities.
Carers Queensland is the peak body for unpaid carers in Queensland. The aim of this campaign is to promote the role of unpaid carers in our communities and to help those who do not identify as a carer, to self-identify and reach out for celebrate services

This Light Up is organised by: Carer's Queensland

item.title: International Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness
item.description:
Thursday, 15 October 2026

Victoria Bridge will be lit Blue and Pink to support International Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness

International Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness Month honours the babies who have died during pregnancy, birth or infancy and recognises the enduring impact of loss on parents, siblings, grandparents and loved ones. The campaign seeks to raise awareness, encourage open conversations about pregnancy and infant loss, foster a compassionate community, and ensure bereaved families feel seen, supported and remembered. Illuminating Brisbane landmarks in pink and blue provides a meaningful public tribute and demonstrates community support for those affected.

This Light Up is organised by: Mater Mother's Hospital

item.title: Developmental Language Disorder Awareness Day
item.description:
Friday, 16 October 2026

Kangaroo Point Bridge will be lit Purple to support Developmental Language Disorder Awareness Day

DLD Day is Friday 16 October. The purpose of this awareness campaign is to increase public understanding of Developmental Language Disorder (DLD), a common but often hidden condition that affects a person’s ability to understand and use spoken language. By lighting the Story Bridge, the campaign aims to visually highlight DLD, spark community conversation, reduce stigma, and promote inclusion. It seeks to educate families, educators, health professionals, and the wider community about the challenges faced by people with DLD and the importance of early identification and support.

This Light Up is organised by: DLD Project Foundation

item.title: Eve of Melt Festival River Pride Parade and Brisbane Pride Festival
item.description:
Friday, 23 October 2026

Reddacliff Place sculptures will be lit all colours to celebrate the Eve of Melt Festival River Pride Parade and Brisbane Pride Festival

River Pride Parade will set sail and help make Brisbane River/Maiwar sparkle with pride in the dazzling rainbow flotilla. Celebrating all our LGBTQIA+ communities and allies in true Brisbane style… by boat! From yachts to jetskis, join the colourful flotilla cruising from West End to Brisbane Powerhouse as part of the MELT Festival.
